findings.subtopic: Special legal basis for personal-data use in AI development
findings.ai_system_type: AI systems developed using personal data
findings.effective_date: Six months after promulgation; exact date pending promulgation
findings.what_changed: South Korea's National Assembly passed an amendment creating a special route to use lawfully collected personal data for AI development when pseudonymous or anonymous data are insufficient, public or social necessity is recognized, strengthened safeguards apply, and PIPC review and resolution are obtained.
findings.previous_position: Use of lawfully collected personal data for a different purpose generally required separate consent, another statutory basis, or conversion to pseudonymous or anonymous data; selected AI projects relied on time-limited regulatory sandboxes.
findings.new_position: The passed amendment adds a dedicated AI-development pathway, subject to necessity conditions, strengthened safeguards, PIPC approval, risk assessment for higher-impact processing, and transparency through privacy notices and PIPC publication.
findings.legal_significance: The amendment would create a new statutory processing route and replaces reliance on case-specific, time-limited sandbox exceptions for qualifying AI development. It still requires Cabinet consideration, promulgation, and a six-month commencement period.
findings.business_significance: Qualifying developers may gain a durable route to use higher-quality personal data, but must prepare evidence of necessity, safeguards, PIPC review materials, risk assessment where applicable, and public disclosures.
findings.technical_significance: AI-data pipelines should support necessity testing, access controls, strengthened safeguards, risk assessment, traceability, and disclosure of use under the special route.
